author: Joyce Ramirez
title: Apple (AAPL) Stake Boosted by 440 Investment Group LLC
text:
Posted by Joyce Ramirez on Apr 17th, 2018 // No Comments 
440 Investment Group LLC grew its stake in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 28.1% in the fourth quarter, according to the company in its most recent filing with the SEC. The firm owned 21,345 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after acquiring an additional 4,686 shares during the quarter. Apple comprises about 2.6% of 440 Investment Group LLC’s portfolio, making the stock its 7th biggest holding. 440 Investment Group LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $3,612,000 as of its most recent filing with the SEC. 
Several other large investors also recently added to or reduced their stakes in the company. First Hawaiian Bank increased its holdings in Apple by 24.3% in the 4th quarter. First Hawaiian Bank now owns 7,168 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $1,213,000 after purchasing an additional 1,401 shares in the last quarter. Gemmer Asset Management LLC increased its holdings in Apple by 9.0% in the 4th quarter. Gemmer Asset Management LLC now owns 9,439 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $1,597,000 after purchasing an additional 782 shares in the last quarter. Oakmont Partners LLC increased its holdings in Apple by 10.6% in the 4th quarter. Oakmont Partners LLC now owns 13,971 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $2,364,000 after purchasing an additional 1,335 shares in the last quarter. Banced Corp increased its holdings in Apple by 6.0% in the 4th quarter. Banced Corp now owns 14,079 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $2,383,000 after purchasing an additional 802 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Inspirion Wealth Advisors LLC increased its holdings in Apple by 5.3% in the 4th quarter. Inspirion Wealth Advisors LLC now owns 13,858 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $2,345,000 after purchasing an additional 698 shares in the last quarter. Hedge funds and other institutional investors own 61.35% of the company’s stock. 
In other Apple news, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of Apple stock in a transaction dated Tuesday, April 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total transaction of $11,564,692.22. The sale was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is accessible through the SEC website . Also, SVP Daniel J. Riccio sold 17,375 shares of Apple stock in a transaction dated Wednesday, April 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $169.12, for a total value of $2,938,460.00. Following the sale, the senior vice president now directly owns 66,191 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $11,194,221.92. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . In the last ninety days, insiders have sold 125,988 shares of company stock valued at $21,336,201. Corporate insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock. 
NASDAQ:AAPL opened at $175.82 on Tuesday. The firm has a market cap of $886,582.31, a P/E ratio of 17.96, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.32 and a beta of 1.25. Apple has a 52-week low of $140.45 and a 52-week high of $183.50. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a current ratio of 1.24 and a quick ratio of 1.20. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last issued its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, topping the Thomson Reuters’ consensus estimate of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a return on equity of 37.37% and a net margin of 21.13%. The firm had revenue of $88.29 billion during the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $87.62 billion. During the same quarter in the previous year, the company posted $3.36 earnings per share. The company’s revenue was up 12.7% compared to the same quarter last year. equities research analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.37 EPS for the current year. 
Several brokerages have recently weighed in on AAPL. UBS set a $190.00 price target on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research note on Friday, January 5th. Morgan Stanley reissued a “buy” rating and issued a $205.00 price target (up previously from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a research note on Tuesday, January 23rd. Sanford C. Bernstein cut Apple from an “outperform” rating to a “market perform” rating and decreased their price target for the company from $195.00 to $170.00 in a research note on Friday, February 2nd. HSBC set a $204.00 target price on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Tuesday, January 30th. Finally, Vetr raised Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $184.49 target price for the company in a research note on Monday, March 5th. Two research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-two have issued a buy rating and one has given a strong buy rating to the stock. The stock currently has an average rating of “Buy” and an average target price of $203.21. Apple Company Profile 
Apple Inc (Apple) designs, manufactures and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, and portable digital music players, and a variety of related software, services, peripherals, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications. The Company’s products and services include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple TV, a portfolio of consumer and professional software applications, the iOS and OS X operating systems, iCloud, and a variety of accessory, service and support offerings.
